original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the ground equipment required to enable optical communication with spacecrafts at low elevation angles,including Optical Ground Station (OGS) downlink fibre coupling and Pointing, Acquisition  Tracking (PAT) sequence elements.TargetedImprovements:The target improvement for LEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase of theoperation time by a factor of two. The target improvement forGEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase the usable spatial coverage of the GEO satellite by a factor of two.Description: To date, numerous optical satellite communication links have beensuccessfully demonstrated. Most of these experiments have operated at elevationangles exceeding 25 degrees to overcome significantatmospheric propagation challenges, such as intense turbulence. However, for LEO satellites,about half of their visibility in a circular orbit occurs between 5 and 25 elevation. Therefore, overcoming challenges with low elevation optical links coulddouble operation time. For GEO satellites, the elevation angle remains constant; however, enabling low-elevation links can potentially double thesatellite's spatial coverage on Earth. Moreover, improvements in low-elevation optical links have significant impact on both classical and quantumcommunications.This activity will examine the necessary techniques and develop the required hardware to facilitatelow elevation optical communication links through theatmosphere. This will involve namely: Study the required techniques to enable low elevation links and provide trade-off analysis Design and develop the PAT  fibre-coupled receiver systems of an OGS that enables optical communication links at low elevations Integrate the optical PAT/receiver systems to an identified OGS Perform an experimental link campaign at low elevations Analysis of the obtained results and conclude on a way forward towards higher TRL of the technology developed under this contract.

original.description: A new approach to engineering, sustaining and third-level maintenance is proposed for the Back-End installations at the Deep Spacesites in New Norcia, Cebreros, and Malarge, the Near-Earth sites in Kiruna and Kourou, and the Ground Station Reference Facility(GSRF) at ESOC. Under this approach, following a successful phase-in, the end-to-end responsibility for these installations shall betaken over by the prime contractor. The term Back-End refers in the ESTRACK terminology to the systems integrating the Tracking,Telemetry, Command Processor, the ground systems test and validation infrastructure, Frequency and Timing subsystem and the IT infrastructure of the ground stations. The contractual scope of this procurement proposal includes integration and sustaining activities, predictive and corrective maintenance of the various backend subsystems and subsystem retests, spares and repair procurement and third-level support to the Maintenance and Operations (MO) teams for all ESTRACK terminals.

original.description: Objective:The identification of Hungarian industry / academia capabilities and interests in optical communication technologies, and a survey / test campaign of Hungarian infrastructures in view of finding potential locations for optical ground stationsTargeted Improvements:Selection of optimum optical ground infrastructure sites for participation in optical and quantum communication programsDescription:This activity will identify the capabilities and interests of Hungarian industry and academia in optical communication technologies and survey existing Hungarian infrastructures in view of finding potential locations for optical ground stations. The survey needs to identify Hungarian companies and academia suited to perform small prototyping projects with minimal administrative burden. In addition, the Makerspace will conduct a study on Hungarian potential to develop and operate a network of optical ground stations: aspects to be investigated include, but are not limited to, e.g. the optimum location of potential optical ground stations, the daily and seasonal cloudiness level of the sites, the atmospheric seeing conditions, the sky brightness mainly during thenight, but also during the day. Other topics related to optical and quantum communication development will also be made possible with this activity.The activity will specifically involve small industrial players throughout Hungary, which are at present focused on terrestrial consumer-oriented telecommunication projects.A prime contractor will be responsible for managing the separate individual development contracts. This prime will coordinate and manage all Makerspace activities, and oversee the prototyping projects/surveys. Initially, one activity will be defined by ESA and requested as part of the Statement of Work.The subsequent projects/activities will be jointly defined by ESA and the prime contractor, during the course of the activity. This will allow aligning the activities with the national developments and interests. The activities will target SMEs and industries that do not usually engage with ESA.

original.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.
